OPA rent ceilings for the Detroit area were upheld in two decisions by the E. S. Emergency Court of Appeals Saturday.


The court ruled against a petition by the Detroit Property Owners Association seeking to smash the ceilings.


At the same time it decided, in a complaint brought by the Equitable Trust Co. of Detroit, that landlords' profits here are higher now than before the war.


The court was set up purposely to decide appeals from decisions by OPA administrators.


"We are not certain whether we will appeal to the Supreme Court," said Karl Smith, president of the Property Owners Association. "We have not read the decision."


Raymond Paul, chief OPA attorney, said such an appeal must be started within 30 days.
